root_cause_identification.expected_solution: Agent must identify that Flux v2.2 / helm-controller v0.37 changed the HelmRelease status condition API. helm-controller's reconciliation pipeline (internal/controller/helmrelease_controller.go and internal/reconcile/release.go, with HelmRelease type definitions in api/v2beta2/helmrelease_types.go) reads and writes status conditions in the new format after a successful release. HelmRelease resources that were in-progress during the v0.36 -> v0.37 upgrade retain old-format conditions, and the new reconciler in internal/controller/helmrelease_controller.go cannot interpret them, so it perpetually treats the release as not ready and re-reconciles in a loop. The symptom is observed through the Flux CLI: cmd/flux/get_helmrelease.go imports helm-controller's api/v2beta2 and reads item.Status.Conditions to render the Ready column that shows Ready=False.
evaluation_criteria: Names internal/controller/helmrelease_controller.go (helm-controller) as the reconciler that misparses old-format conditions
Names internal/reconcile/release.go (helm-controller) as the writer of new-format conditions
References api/v2beta2/helmrelease_types.go (helm-controller) as the type/API surface that changed
Explains the version-mismatch mechanism: stale old-format conditions left on in-progress HelmRelease resources after the upgrade
Identifies why this produces an infinite reconcile loop rather than a transient error

error_chain_trace.expected_solution: Error chain: (1) An operator runs `flux get helmreleases` and sees the affected releases as Ready=False. (2) The Flux CLI reader cmd/flux/get_helmrelease.go reads item.Status.Conditions to render that Ready column, so the stale condition is what it displays. (3) The HelmRelease was in-progress when helm-controller was upgraded from v0.36 to v0.37 (Flux v2.1 -> v2.2), leaving an old-format condition. (4) helm-controller's internal/reconcile/release.go successfully deploys the release and writes new-format status conditions defined in api/v2beta2/helmrelease_types.go. (5) The reconciler internal/controller/helmrelease_controller.go reads the status conditions and cannot parse the old format, so it treats the release as not ready. (6) The reconciler triggers another reconciliation, producing an infinite loop. (7) kustomize-controller and other consumers that depend on HelmRelease readiness are also blocked.
evaluation_criteria: Starts the chain at the flux CLI readout: cmd/flux/get_helmrelease.go (flux2) reads Status.Conditions to display Ready=False
Mentions the helm-controller v0.36 -> v0.37 (Flux v2.1 -> v2.2) upgrade as the trigger for in-progress HelmReleases retaining old-format conditions
Identifies helm-controller writing new-format conditions and the same controller's reconciler reading them as the seam
Describes the infinite reconcile loop and the downstream impact on kustomize-controller

affected_resources.expected_solution: Affected components: the Flux CLI readout cmd/flux/get_helmrelease.go, which renders the Ready column operators observe from item.Status.Conditions; the helm-controller reconciler that parses status conditions (internal/controller/helmrelease_controller.go); the helm-controller release writer that emits new-format conditions (internal/reconcile/release.go); the HelmRelease v2beta2 API surface (api/v2beta2/helmrelease_types.go and api/v2beta2/condition_types.go); all HelmRelease resources that were in-progress during the v0.36 to v0.37 helm-controller upgrade; kustomize-controller and other consumers that gate on HelmRelease readiness.
evaluation_criteria: Names cmd/flux/get_helmrelease.go (flux2) as the CLI readout surfacing the not-ready status
Mentions HelmRelease resources that were in-progress during the upgrade as affected
Mentions a downstream consumer such as kustomize-controller

remediation_proposal.expected_solution: Add backward-compatible status condition parsing in helm-controller's reconciler (internal/controller/helmrelease_controller.go) so it accepts both old and new condition formats. For immediate operational relief, manually delete and recreate the affected HelmRelease resources or annotate them to force a full status condition reset.
evaluation_criteria: Identifies an operational workaround (recreate or annotate affected HelmRelease resources)
Addresses the parser/writer skew rather than only suppressing the symptom
